expectations.evidence: The transcript names 'the register the culture work set' as one of the interview questions it has not asked, and says the answers could change the design. That shows it knows the register matters. It never actually asks the user which register was set. It never ties the redesigned closing moment to that register either. It keeps the confetti and adds whole-room acknowledgement, both its own tone choices made without checking them against the culture work. Acknowledging the gap is only partial credit.

expectations.evidence: The transcript never asks what tone or register the conference's culture work has already set, such as playful, understated or inclusive. It doesn't check whether confetti, a surprise stage moment or a ribbon fits that register. It critiques the peak moment only on audience (first-timers versus contributors), consent, selection and logistics. Its fixes (bring first-timers on stage, show photos and quotes, use biodegradable confetti) choose a celebratory tone without anchoring it to an existing register. No clarifying question on culture or tone appears; the only questions asked concern the rep
